newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece to cut EFTE loan tax to 3.0 pct - govt source.
newsitem.headline: Greece to cut EFTE loan tax to 3.0 pct - govt source.

text.p: Greece's economic committee decided late on Wednesday night to cut the special tax on banking services (EFTE) to 3.0 percent from 4.0 percent currently, a high-level national economy ministry source told Reuters.
The EFTE tax is levied currently on interest payments on drachma loans.

The committee, headed by National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou, also decided to slap the lower EFTE tax on all types of loans including forex loans as well as loans syndicated by foreign banks, the source said.
A legislative amendment is required for the decision to go into effect and this is expected to take place in the next few months, probably before summer, the source said.
The economic committee also decided to increase the contribution of Law 128 to 1.2 percent from 1.0 percent for all types of loans, drachma or forex, he added.
The contribution based on law 128 was enacted to raise money for relief to earthquake stricken areas in the early 1980s.
The government is trying to make foreign currency denominated loans carrying lower interest rates less attractive for local companies and individuals.

Development Minister Vasso Papandreou, Agriculture Minister Stefanos Tzoumakas, Labour Minister Miltiadis Papaioannou as well as deputy ministers participate in the committee. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
